newsitem.title: INDIA: Fire engulfs building in Indian capital, no deaths.
newsitem.headline: Fire engulfs building in Indian capital, no deaths.

text.p: A fire broke out in a tall building in the central business district of the Indian capital on Tuesday, but there were no reports of casualties.
Police said no one was believed to be trapped in the fire that started on the ninth floor before offices opened in the Chanderlok Building of New Delhi's Connaught Place area.
The fire, which came four days after smoke from a blaze killed 57 people in a packed movie theatre, was still burning three hours after it started.
The ninth floor houses one of the offices of Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd, which provides telephone services in New Delhi and Bombay.

Authorities said it was unlikely that anyone was trapped inside the 10-storey building, which caught fire at 9 a.m. (0330 GMT) before offices opened. One person died in a fire in the same building in 1995, officials said.
The fire followed last Friday's major blaze at South Delhi's Uphaar Grand cinema hall that killed 57 people.

The yellow and grey building also houses the offices of the State Bank of India, Shipping Corporation of India, Essar Group, the tourism offices of several northern Indian states and Japan Airlines Co Ltd.
Fire officials said strong winds were fanning the blaze.

"If the wind gets any stronger the fire will spread," a fireman said. There were more than a dozen fire tenders at the scene trying to put out the flames, which by late morning were still licking the upper storey.
The Chanderlok building is owned by New Delhi Municipal Corporation (NDMC). A NDMC spokesman said that the building had not been certified safe as it did not have a fire escape.
